Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Emerson Delgado
Member ID: W249568388 (three-letter prefix: [not provided in records on file — please confirm from ID card])
Plan: Simply Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), Florida
Denied Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-25
Reference Number: POC-926BF4D7E4-25977
Treating Surgeon: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-25, which denied prior authorization for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827). The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." This letter, together with the enclosed records, is submitted to respond directly to that stated reason.

As instructed in your published appeals procedure, I am including the following: my name, address, and phone number; my identification number; the name of my treating provider; the dates of service at issue; and the claim/reference number for the decision I am disputing (POC-926BF4D7E4-25977). Your appeals procedure states that "A written Appeal must state plainly the reason(s) why the Member disagrees with Our claim decision, Our refusal to authorize or cover a requested service or supply, or how We calculated the benefit," and that "The Appeal should include any pertinent documents and medical records not originally submitted with the claim or request for the service or supply and any other information that the Member feels may have a bearing on the decision." I am doing so below.

Policy applied to this request: In researching the medical-necessity criteria your plan uses for CPT 29827, I located a document titled "Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. 228: Shoulder Surgeries" (SUR228), effective December 1, 2025, last reviewed October 2025, published on a document library used by the Wellpoint/Elevance Health enterprise, of which Simply Healthcare Plans, Inc. (d/b/a Wellpoint Florida, Inc.) is a part. I was not able to independently confirm, through Simply's provider portal, that this exact version of SUR228 is the specific policy adopted for my contract. If a different policy or clinical guideline was actually used to review my request, I am formally requesting that you identify that document and send me a copy, consistent with your stated obligation to provide, "upon request and free of charge, reasonable access to, and copies of, all documents, records, and other information relevant to the Member's request" that were relied upon in making the adverse determination.

To the extent SUR228 is the applicable policy, it states: "Rotator cuff repair may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.)." I address each criterion below with the corresponding evidence from my medical record.

Criterion A: "Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and"
— Supporting evidence: I have had 18 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest. I am currently unable to lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. This functional loss is documented in my surgeon's clinical notes and the physical therapy discharge note.

Criterion B: "Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear and has associated function limiting pain; and"
— Supporting evidence: I completed a course of NSAIDs over approximately 8 months with inadequate relief; a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30 gave only 4 weeks of partial relief; and I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics from 2026-05-10 through 2026-07-05, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. Taken together, this non-surgical management program spans well over three months and includes both physical therapy and a trial of anti-inflammatory medication and a cortisone injection, without adequate resolution of symptoms.

Criterion C: "Individual meets all of the following Criteria (1. and 2.) on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Either of the following: a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs: a. Drop Arm Test; or b. Painful Arc Test; or c. Jobe or Empty Can Test; or d. External Rotation Lag Sign (Dropping Sign); or e. Internal Rotation Lag Sign; or f. Lift-Off Test; or g. Bear Hug Test; or h. Belly-Press Test (Napoleon); or i. Belly-Off Test; or j. Neer Impingement Test; or k. Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement; or l. Hornblower Test (Patte); and"
— Supporting evidence: My surgeon's examination documents range of motion limited by pain and positive provocative testing on the affected side compared with the unaffected side. The clinical summary provided to me for this appeal does not identify the specific named test(s) performed (e.g., [name of specific positive orthopedic test(s) — Drop Arm, Neer, Hawkins-Kennedy, or other, to be confirmed from Dr. Duval's exam note]). I am requesting that Dr. Duval's office supplement the record with the specific test name(s) and results to fully document this criterion, and I will forward that information as soon as it is available.

Criterion D: "Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings."
— Supporting evidence: MRI of the shoulder performed 2026-06-18 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This finding is consistent with, and corroborates, my reported 18-month history of progressive pain and documented functional limitations described above.

Additional relevant history: I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder; my BMI is 29; and I am a non-smoker.

Enclosed with this appeal are the following records, which were the basis for the above statements and which I ask you to review in full:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-10 to 2026-07-05, 16 visits)
- Medication/treatment history documenting NSAID trial (approximately 8 months) and corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-30
- MRI report dated 2026-06-18
- Surgeon's (Dr. Duval, MD) clinical/examination notes
- [Any additional records the practice can supply identifying the specific positive orthopedic test(s) performed]

Given this documentation, I ask that you reverse the denial of CPT 29827 and approve the requested rotator cuff repair. If any specific item is still considered missing or insufficient, your appeals procedure states that your written determination "shall include instructions for requesting copies of any referenced evidence, documents or clinical review information not already provided to the Member," and I ask that you identify precisely what remains missing so it can be supplied promptly.

I understand from your appeals procedure that "An Appeal of an adverse determination must be sent within 180 calendar days of the date the finding was made," and I am submitting this appeal well within that period (the notice states a deadline of 2027-02-21).

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the name and contact information of the reviewer assigned to my case. If my clinical situation should be treated as urgent, please advise me of the process for requesting an expedited review.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Emerson Delgado
Member ID: W249568388

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note; medication/injection records; MRI report dated 2026-06-18; surgeon's clinical notes; [additional exam documentation, if provided by Dr. Duval's office]
